To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the average number of wounded quarks in a given collision can be related to the mass of the colliding nuclei and the center-of-mass collision energy, and that the average number collisions of wounded quarks can be related to a universal parameter which is a function of the collision energy.

the average charged multiplicity 〈n〉, the central pseudorapidity density 〈dη/dη=0〉, and the complete rapididity dependence of dn/dy are all well described by the same model, and that this model also explains how 〈n〉, 〈dη/dy〉 and dn/dy vary with the mass number A of colliding nuclei and with √sNN and centrality.

we have proposed a phenomenological model based on wounded quark interactions for describing the charged particle multiplicities at relativistic ion collider experiments and that the results of our model are well supported by available experimental data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the average charged particle production in relativistic heavy ion collisions and its interrelation with the p-p and p-A collisions.
the study of the multiplicity production at relativistic ion collisions.
the development of a simple phenomenological model to explain the charged particle multiplicity in relativistic heavy ion collisions.

the wounded quarks picture provides an excellent description of the multiplicity data at RHIC and LHC energies.
the model proposed in this paper can be used to explain the average multiplicity and the complete rapidty dependence of dn/dy for relativistic heavy-ion collisions.
the wounded quark model provides an excellent description for the charged particle multiplicity and its variations with collision energy and system size in relativistic heavy ion collisions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the wounded quark model can be extended to describe the multiplicity in A-A collisions.

the model is able to describe the average multiplicity in A-A collisions in a wide range of energies (√sNN=4.2–200 GeV) and centralities (0–80%), and the model predictions for √sNN=5.5 TeV are in good agreement with the experimental results.
we have developed a simple parameterization which can explain the average charged particle production in p-p, p-A and A-A collisions at relativistic ion collider experiments.
